text: Exuberant means bursting with joyful energy and showing it, like a team piling together after a goal. Here the exuberant fans are so wildly excited at a match that beer gets splashed around, so the jersey needed a tough fabric.

Something obscure is known to very few people or hard to notice. The word first meant dark or hidden. Here, wearing merch for something obscure works like a secret handshake, because only fellow fans will recognise it.
Bespoke means made specially for one person instead of bought ready-made, like a suit cut to your exact size. Here it describes cups and t-shirts that people design for their own parties.

A mania is a huge, wild craze that sweeps over lots of people at once, so that they all want the same thing badly. Tulips and Pokemon cards have both caused manias. The writer says the tote-bag rush is one of the strangest.
Tulips are spring flowers. In the 1600s in the Netherlands, people went so wild for them that single bulbs sold for the price of a house. That makes them the classic example of a craze.

Beanie Babies are small stuffed toys that became a huge collecting craze in the 1990s. People bought them hoping they would become valuable later. The article lists them as another example of a craze.
A craze is a sudden, short-lived wave of excitement about something, like a toy or a fashion everyone wants. The craze for mini totes has shoppers lining up outside stores.
Trader Joe's is an American grocery chain known for its own-brand foods and cheerful shops. Its mini tote bags are what set off the craze this article describes.
Limited-time means only available for a short window, after which it is gone. Shops use it because people hurry to buy when they know a thing will not last.
A queue is a line of people waiting their turn. It is the usual word in British English, where Americans would say line. Huge queues formed outside shops for the bags.
To impose a rule is to put it in place and make people follow it, whether they like it or not. Some stores imposed a limit on how many bags each customer can buy.
Strict means firm and not bending, like a strict teacher who never lets late homework slide. A strict limit means the shop really will not let anyone buy more.
Resale means selling something you already bought, usually to someone else. Resale websites let people list items at any price, which is why a $2.99 bag shows up for $20 or even $50,000.
Wishful means hoping for something that probably will not happen. A wishful price is one the seller dreams of getting. A bag for $50,000 is wishful because nobody will actually pay it.
Merchandise means goods that are bought and sold in a store. In this article it mostly means items with a brand's name or logo on them, like shirts and mugs.
Merch is short for merchandise. It usually means items such as t-shirts, hats and bags with a logo, band, team or shop on them.
Trendy means fashionable right now, and is often used for things that may soon go out of style. The writer calls merch the trendy term.
Oxford Economics is a research company that studies money and business. The article uses its estimate that people around the world spend $338 billion a year on merch.
A licensed product carries a famous name, like a movie character, with permission from the owner, usually in return for a fee. Licensed products are one kind of merch.
Print-on-demand means an item is only printed once someone orders it, so the seller does not need to store piles of them. Many online shops make t-shirts this way.
To peddle is to try to sell things, often by going around from place to place. The word can sound a bit unimpressed. Here many kinds of companies are peddling merch.
Wares are things that someone has for sale. You may hear a market seller showing off his wares. Here it means the merch the companies sell.

Palantir is a technology company that sells data-analysis software, mostly to governments and big businesses. It is not the kind of firm you would expect to sell clothes, which is why its tennis whites were news.
OpenAI is the company that makes ChatGPT, an artificial-intelligence chatbot. It launched a clothing line, which surprised people and drew some teasing online.
To scoff is to make fun of something in a way that shows you think it is silly. The online user scoffed, saying wearing OpenAI clothes was a good way to get teased.
To bully someone is to pick on or mock them again and again. Here the joke is that wearing the clothing would get you mocked.
To fork out money is to pay for something, usually when you are not very happy about the price. Parents often fork out for the toy their child wants.
Elsa is the snow queen from Disney's movie Frozen. Elsa dresses are among the best-selling costumes for young children, so they are a classic example of merch for kids.
Buzz Lightyear is a toy space ranger who is a main character in Pixar's Toy Story movies. Buzz toys are a classic example of merch.
To splash out is to spend a lot of money on something fun, more than you normally would. Fans of a singer might splash out on tour merch.
Barclays is a big British bank. Its analysts studied how much concert fans would spend, as shown by the 100 pounds estimate in the article.
Harry Styles is a British pop singer who first became famous in the band One Direction. His fans are known for buying lots of tour merch.
If a place is awash in something, it is covered in it, as if flooded by water. New York is awash in blue and orange, meaning you can see those colours on clothes everywhere.
Apparel is a formal word for clothing. Sports teams sell lots of apparel with their colours and logo.
The Knicks are New York City's professional basketball team, and their colours are blue and orange. The article says the city is full of their gear.
Victorious means having won. The Knicks are the city's victorious team, so fans are eager to wear their colours.
Arsenal is a famous English football (soccer) club in the Premier League, which is England's top division. It earns a lot of money from selling its shirts and other merch.
In British English, kit means the clothes a sports team plays in. That is the same thing Americans call a uniform or jersey. Here Arsenal's kit sales grew by 26 percent.
Making or buying in bulk means in very large amounts at once, which usually makes each item cheaper. A tote bag costs under a dollar to make in bulk.
A life cycle is all the stages of something's life from start to end. A tote's life cycle is the long time it gets carried around before it wears out.
The literati are people who love books and reading, often the most devoted readers. The article says the literati love totes from Daunt Books and Shakespeare and Company.
In business, eyeballs is a casual way to say people looking at something. The more eyeballs a bag gets, the more people see the shop's name.
Shakespeare and Company is a famous English-language bookshop in Paris, known for its tote bags. Visitors love carrying them as a souvenir.
Lidl is a European supermarket chain. It surprised people by releasing a funny football jersey.
A parody is a funny imitation of something serious, copying its style to make people laugh. Lidl's jersey copied the look of the England shirt as a joke.
In British English, a team's strip is the set of clothes it wears to play. Here a parody strip means a joke version of the England shirt.
Fabric is cloth, the material that clothes are made from. Lidl chose a fabric that resists liquids and smells.
Odour is the British spelling of odor, a smell, usually an unpleasant one. An odour-resistant fabric does not hold onto bad smells.
If something sold out, every single one was bought and none are left. The Lidl jersey sold out in 55 seconds, which shows how eager fans were.
To spur something is to push it to happen faster, like a rider tapping a horse. The writer says the trend was spurred by the pandemic.
Beloved means loved very much by people. A beloved local business is one the neighbourhood really cares about.
Signalling means showing others something about yourself without saying it, such as what you like or where you belong. Wearing a band's shirt signals to others that you are a fan.
Psychology is the study of how people think and feel. Consumer psychology is about why people buy what they buy.
Individuality is what makes you different from everyone else. Many young people use merch to show their individuality.
Status is how highly other people see you. In the past, status came from expensive things. The expert says it now comes more from taste and belonging.
A consultancy is a company whose experts give advice to other businesses for a fee. Tracksuit, which is mentioned here, is a brand consultancy.
Counter-intuitively means in a way that seems backward at first. Wearing something to stand out should make you less like the crowd, but it also links you to a community.
A community is a group of people who share a place or an interest. A band's shirt can show that you belong to the group of fans.
Civic means to do with a town or the people who live in it. A civic organisation is a local group such as a volunteer club.
Atomised means broken into tiny separate pieces, like atoms. A society that is atomised is one where people are split up and alone instead of joined in groups.

t: small fish in a big pond
forms: small fish in a big pond
text: Being a small fish in a big pond means being one very ordinary person among many. The expert adds that small fish can find each other, meaning fans of an obscure thing can spot one another.
A knowing nod is a small nod that says I understand what you mean. A stranger who spots your merch might give you one.
A hen do is the British name for a party held for a woman before her wedding. Americans would call it a bachelorette party.
Etsy is a website where people sell handmade or custom-made things. It makes it easy to create bespoke merch.
Party favours are small gifts handed to guests as a thank-you for coming. Birthday bags of goodies are an example.
Swag is slang for free or cheap goods with a logo, such as pens and caps, handed out by a company. The article uses it as another word for merch.
Architectural Digest is a magazine about beautiful homes and interior design. It asked whether a home should have its own merch.
A souvenir is an object you keep to remember a place or event, like a mug from a trip. The more people value experiences, the more they want souvenirs.
To cotton on is to finally understand something. The ending line says everyone has cottoned on to how good merch is.
